top_stories.title: 'The Donald of Dubai': UAE billionaire close to Trump bets $66 billion on AI to become the world's data king - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Hussain Sajwani**, chairman of **DAMAC Properties**, is investing billions of dollars in data centers, aiming to become a global leader in the field.  Sajwani, who attended Donald Trump's inauguration and is on Forbes' Arab rich-list, saw an opportunity during the COVID-19 pandemic to pivot from real estate to data centers, spurred by the growth of cloud computing and AI. He has earmarked sites in 13 countries across multiple continents, with a total capacity of 6,000 megawatts and a projected cost of $66 billion. Sajwani believes the demand for data center space will continue to grow rapidly due to the rise of AI and hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google.

top_stories.title: Zee Entertainment to raise $241 million for stategic initiatives - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Zee Entertainment** announced plans to raise funds after securing a deal with **FIFA** for the 2026 World Cup broadcast rights in India. The company, which has expanded its sports broadcasting portfolio and invested in other ventures like micro-drama app Bullet and visual effects studio PhantomFX, reported a loss in the March quarter due to higher expenses and advertising budget constraints.  The fundraise comes after uncertainty surrounding the tournament's availability in India.

top_stories.title: Indian national Sandeep Singh arrested by ICE in California, wanted in Germany for attempted murder; may face deportation - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **ICE** arrested **Sandeep Singh**, a 40-year-old Indian national, in California for attempted murder in Germany.  Singh illegally entered the U.S. from Mexico in 2023 and is currently being held in ICE detention while immigration proceedings continue. Authorities have not provided details about the German warrant or the case. **ICE** has detained several other Indian nationals in recent years, primarily those with criminal records.

top_stories.title: Congress approaches Supreme Court over Meenakshi Natarajan nomination rejection | India News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Congress** challenged the rejection of its candidate, **Meenakshi Natarajan**, for the Rajya Sabha election in Madhya Pradesh. The party filed a petition with the Supreme Court after an objection was raised by **Rahul Kothari**, a BJP state general secretary.  They argued that the returning officer's (RO) order disqualifying Natarajan should be withdrawn as there is no criminal case against her, and she did not have to disclose details of a private complaint in her affidavit. The Congress delegation requested the Election Commission to exercise its constitutional power under Article 324 to intervene and set aside the RO's order.

top_stories.title: Gujarat Confidential: ‘In-charge’, in line | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Gujarat** has seen a revolving door of in-charge Directors General of Police (DGP) over the past 13 years.  After several interim appointments, **Pramod Kumar** served as in-charge DGP for two stints before retiring in March 2018. The state then saw three full-time DGPs: **Shivanand Jha**, **Ashish Bhatia**, and **Vikas Sahay**. All three received extensions to their tenures.

top_stories.title: On-duty traffic cop injured after being hit by speeding car in Southeast Delhi | Delhi News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: A **Delhi Police** head constable, Rahul Kumar, sustained injuries after being struck by a speeding car driving from the wrong side of the road in Sarai Jullena on Tuesday morning. The incident occurred while Kumar was on duty at a red light.  The offending vehicle fled the scene, leaving Kumar injured. A case has been registered against the driver under relevant sections of the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** and the **Motor Vehicles Act**.

top_stories.title: Trump administration cracks down on ‘birth tourism’, revokes hundreds of visas: 'No foreigner is permitted...' - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The US State Department** has intensified enforcement against "birth tourism," revoking hundreds of visas and targeting organized networks facilitating childbirth trips for citizenship. The department claims to have identified over 600 cases across multiple regions, including West Africa, Europe, and North Africa, where individuals used fraudulent documents and visa brokers to enter the country. **The US** is tightening controls to protect the integrity of its immigration system and prevent misuse of visitor visas.  This crackdown aligns with previous efforts under the Trump administration to reduce fraud within the immigration system.

top_stories.title: 3 Indians missing after attack on ship, Delhi summons US diplomat | India News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **India** summoned the US charge d'affaires, **Jason Meeks**, following an attack on a commercial ship off the coast of Oman that left three Indian crew members missing. The incident is the first since President Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025 and follows similar incidents involving Indian seafarers in recent months.  **India** condemned the attack, calling for de-escalation of tensions and the restoration of peace and stability in the region. The **Indian Ministry of External Affairs** reiterated its concerns about attacks on shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region.

top_stories.title: Cyber fraud linked to over 159 cases across country unearthed, nearly Rs 67.92 cr routed through mule account | Delhi News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Officers** at the East Delhi Cyber Police Station arrested a deputy manager of the **National Urban Cooperative Bank** for allegedly facilitating the opening of a mule account used to receive and route proceeds from over 159 cyber fraud cases across the country. The account, registered in the name of Mahakal Enterprises and purportedly belonging to Shailendra Kumar Yadav, was linked to complaints filed on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP). Investigations revealed that the deputy manager did not visit the bank branch during the account opening period and his signatures did not match those on the forms.  Further investigation is underway to determine if a wider network is involved.

top_stories.title: A Meta Employee Who Just Lost Their Job Was Detained by Immigration Agents | WIRED
top_stories.rephrased_article: A former **Meta** employee, who was laid off in May, is reported to have been detained by **US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)**.  The current status of the detained worker is unknown. Internal company communications indicate they were potentially detained in El Paso, Texas, a major US-Mexico border crossing point. This incident has sparked concerns among some employees about the lack of support from **Meta** for immigrant workers facing potential deportation by ICE.
